Django News Application
  • REST API endpoints

REST API endpoints

The REST API is served under /api/ and is built with Django REST Framework. Routes are defined in news.api_urls, and the views are documented in news.api.views.

Authentication

Every endpoint except /api/token/ needs an API token. Request one with a username and password:

Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post -Uri http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/token/ `
    -ContentType "application/json" `
    -Body '{"username": "demo_reader", "password": "DemoPass123!"}'

The response looks like {"token": "<your token>"}. Send it on every other request in the Authorization header:

Authorization: Token <your token>

For example, with curl:

curl -H "Authorization: Token <your token>" http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/articles/

Warning

Treat tokens like passwords. Do not commit them or paste them in public.

Endpoints

Method

Path

Allowed roles

Description

POST

/api/token/

Anyone

Exchange a username and password for a token.

GET

/api/articles/

Any signed-in user

List approved articles.

POST

/api/articles/

Journalist

Submit an article (title, content, optional publisher). It starts unapproved.

GET

/api/articles/subscribed/

Reader

Approved articles from the reader’s subscriptions.

GET

/api/articles/<id>/

Any signed-in user

One approved article.

PUT / PATCH

/api/articles/<id>/

Editor, or the journalist who owns it

Update an article. A journalist’s update sends it back for approval.

DELETE

/api/articles/<id>/

Editor, or the journalist who owns it

Delete an article.

GET

/api/publishers/

Any signed-in user

List publishers.

GET

/api/newsletters/

Any signed-in user

List newsletters that contain approved articles.

POST

/api/newsletters/

Editor, journalist

Create a newsletter (title, description, articles).

GET

/api/users/

Any signed-in user

List users (ID, username, role). The email address is included only in the requesting user’s own record.

POST

/api/approved/

Editor

Internal: log an approved article ({"article_id": <id>}).

Requests without a valid token receive 401 Unauthorized; requests from a role that is not allowed receive 403 Forbidden.

Example: submit an article

curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/articles/ \
     -H "Authorization: Token <journalist token>" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"title": "API Story", "content": "Story submitted through the API."}'

Response (201 Created):

{
  "id": 2,
  "title": "API Story",
  "content": "Story submitted through the API.",
  "author": 3,
  "publisher": null,
  "created_at": "2026-01-01T12:00:00-06:00",
  "approved": false
}

Postman collection

postman_collection.json in the project root contains ready-made requests for these endpoints. Import it into Postman, set the base_url and token collection variables, and send the requests.
